title: Runkeeper oncall quirks memo - Zara
content:
Shift log (short and messy) — 2027-02-14
Shift: 07:45–16:00 local
Pager count: 3

1) pg-burst-latency spike (major) — 08:02
- Symptom: sudden 95th pct latency spikes on hosted-generation route (/v1/generate) — p95 ~1200ms -> ~4.8s for ~20min window
- Alert: latency-p95-prod > 1.5s for 5m (SLO red)
- Initial hypothesis: KV cache thrash after model shard rollout + small batch size during morning ramp.
- Quick checks performed:
  • Grafana: tenant: redwood-prod -> spike aligns with two deploys at 07:58 and 08:01 (model variants: gptx-8q and gptx-8q-compat)
  • Node maps: increased cpu_iowait on gpu-host-18, scheduler queue length climbed
  • Runtime logs: repeated "cache-miss -> fallback-kv-regen" lines from inference-runtime (pod: infer-rt-5fdf)
  • Prom: inference_kv_cache_hits dropped 70% for that tenant window
- Immediate mitigation:
  • Rolled back recent canary (deploy/serving-service-canary) at 08:18 — latency returned to baseline by 08:24
  • Scaled up dedicated pool for a 10m burst (autoscaler override) to absorb remaining load (manual: +4 replicas)
- Followups/TODOs:
  [ ] INF-312: add a health-check for KV cache regen rate + alert if regen rate > 50 reqs/min (owner: Priya)
  [ ] Run a staged rollout test that simulates morning ramp (owner: me)
  [ ] Add a pre-deploy step to validate compat model cache warm up in CI (owner: infra-team)
- Notes: we saw a similar pattern last quarter but it was quieter; need to track whether canary selection algorithm put incompatible variant under pressure.

2) tiny auth-service flakiness — 11:14
- Symptom: intermittent 500s from auth-service during token introspection — ~10 requests/min for ~20m
- Quick triage:
  • Logs: heap pressure GC spikes on auth-01 (pod restarted 3x) — JVM OOM? But container wasn't OOMKilled
  • Host metrics: memory usage creeping up after hours of retries; connection_pool exhaustion to redis-tokencache
- Action taken:
  • Restarted auth-01 at 11:28 (replica set), temporarily restored steady 200s
  • Filed SRE-4582 to track root cause (possible leak in tokencache client)
- Followups/TODOs:
  [ ] Add circuit-breaker on tokencache client around auth-service (owner: Andre)
  [ ] Reproduce memory growth with load test (owner: auth-service team)

3) paging noise — 13:40
- Page about increased error-latency from logging pipeline (kinesis->ingest). Turns out it was a noisy customer load pattern; not platform issue. Handed back to growth contact (sarah@growth) with suggested client-side backoff.
- Note: logging/frontend teams to add client sampling guidelines to docs.

Operational notes / oddities observed:
- "Latency smell test" quick heuristic I used today (save this): p50 normal, p95 > 2x p50 and trend upwards over 3 intervals => look at cache + batch size changes + recent deploys. Put this in runbook under "triage heuristics".
- One of the infer-rt pods had a 7s GC pause logged; correlate with model loader churn. Add a gc/loader spike alert.
- Autoscaler didn't kick fast enough when cache regen started — scaling policy for dedicated pools needs re-evaluation for short bursts (<10m).

Action list for next week (prioritized):
1) Short (high impact): add KV-cache regen alert + dashboard tile (Priya).
2) Medium: add canary preflight that does a synthetic warm-up for model variants to ensure low cache-miss rates before traffic (me + infra).
3) Medium: autoscaler tuning for short, high-intensity bursts (SRE + infra).
4) Low: add sampling guide to logging client docs (frontend + growth).

Handoff for next oncall (16:00):
- Status: major incident resolved (rollback done), follow-ups filed (INF-312, SRE-4582). System healthy but monitor p95 for next 12h (morning ramp may show recurrence).
- Quick commands:
  • kubectl get pods -n prod | grep infer-rt
  • kubectl logs infer-rt-5fdf -n prod --since=2h | grep "cache-miss"
  • promql: rate(inference_kv_cache_regens[5m]) > 0.8
- Slack note left in #sre-ops: "Rolled back canary at 08:18 for KV-cache thrash; follow-ups in INF-312 + SRE-4582. Priya owning alerts."

Loose ideas / brainstorms (untested):
- Can we implement a small "cache-warm" preflight that runs in sidecar after deploy and primes KV for top n tenants? Might save the cold-start spike risk.
- Consider a gradual traffic ramp policy tied to cache-hit metric rather than just time. If cache-hit drops below threshold, hold traffic.

Open questions (for follow-up meeting):
- Why did canary selection pick the incompatible variant? (Edge case in selection algorithm?)
- Do we need per-model warm caches (cost vs reliability)?
- Is autoscaler latency due to controller loop interval or cloud-provider API rate limits?

Random log-snippets / short command notes I ran:
- curl -sS "https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/serving/runtime?var-tenant=redwood-prod" | jq '.meta'   # used to confirm deploy times
- kubectl exec -it infer-rt-5fdf -n prod -- /bin/sh -c 'tail -n 200 /var/log/inference/runtime.log | grep -i cache-miss'

Personal TODOs (non-blocking):
- Rerun canary simulation on friday morning (my calendar: Fri 08:30)
- Draft a 1-pager for product about why model variants need cache-warm warming (due Mon)

Final scribble: good quick rollback choice; we need to make this less manual. leave the pager for tonight but ask evening shift to watch p95 for first 2h after any variant deploys.

-- z.p.
